lines.text: ## Architectural stewardship

lines.subject: docs: guide architectural stewardship of subagents
docs: guide architectural stewardship of subagents
lines.text: - Delegate implementation and routine verification, not architectural responsibility. The parent agent's value is big-picture thinking: assess the shape of the code, alignment with user intent, and whether the solution fits verified upstream capabilities and constraints.

lines.subject: docs: guide architectural stewardship of subagents
lines.text: - Use meaningful architectural checkpoints rather than handing off the whole destination unattended. Review the emerging interfaces, domain concepts, reuse, tradeoffs, and evidence; then steer or authorize the next coherent slice. Checkpoints should follow consequential decisions, not arbitrary file-by-file phases.

lines.subject: docs: distinguish trusting checks from reviewing implementation
lines.text: - Trust subagents' reports that they ran their tests and checks; do not routinely rerun the same checks merely to confirm their work. Stay engaged with implementation details: read the code, examine important behaviors and edge cases, and give concrete feedback. Reported passing checks do not replace code review or judgment about whether the checks cover the intended behavior; run additional verification when it answers a specific concern.

lines.subject: docs: guide architectural stewardship of subagents
lines.text: - Ask checkpoint reports to explain what became possible or impossible, which architectural choices were made and why, unresolved tensions, and the proposed next slice, with references. Read the relevant code and evidence rather than approving from summaries alone.

lines.subject: docs: encourage cooperative exploration of broader solutions
lines.text: - Cooperatively anneal broader solutions: balance concrete needs with plausible futures, and use dialogue, implementation evidence, and successive refinement to negotiate the right abstractions. Exploring hypothetical futures is encouraged, not forbidden; make assumptions, costs, and opportunities explicit so the parent, subagents, and user can assess them together. Distinguish paths worth preserving or exploring from capabilities agreed for implementation, and preserve meaningful differences within shared machinery. Let subagents choose coherent implementation slices within the agreed direction.

lines.subject: docs: encourage cooperative exploration of broader solutions
lines.text: - When a possible future would materially change the shape of the solution, consider a focused follow-up question or small exploration to clarify which paths we are building toward, keeping open, or making harder. Bring promising broader directions back for discussion rather than silently implementing or dismissing them.

lines.text: A `doc-pass` is an informal post-writing skill for connecting new work to the existing documentation corpus. It is recommended after most waves of significant weight, once the wave's core argument is written and can guide the search.

lines.subject: AGENTS.md: require model-suffix on wave files, forbid harness names like opencode

lines.text: 1. Identify the new or substantially changed documents and summarize their concepts, claims, vocabulary, and unresolved questions as search terms.

lines.subject: AGENTS.md: require model-suffix on wave files, forbid harness names like opencode
lines.text: 2. Search the containing documentation tree broadly by concept, not only by exact terminology. Check `README.md`, `index.md`, and other indexes first, then use filenames and full-text search to find less obvious relationships.

lines.subject: AGENTS.md: require model-suffix on wave files, forbid harness names like opencode
lines.text: 3. Read enough of each candidate to distinguish a substantive relationship from a keyword collision. Prefer a few explained references over a long undifferentiated link list.

lines.subject: AGENTS.md: require model-suffix on wave files, forbid harness names like opencode
lines.text: 4. Add or update a `Cross-references` section in the new work. Each entry should say why the linked document matters: prior art, supporting evidence, shared vocabulary, tension, contradiction, extension point, or downstream application.

lines.subject: AGENTS.md: require model-suffix on wave files, forbid harness names like opencode
lines.text: 5. Add reciprocal links to older documents when the new work materially changes how they should be navigated or understood. Preserve their original argument rather than opportunistically rewriting them.

lines.text: 6. Maintain the documentation area's `README.md` or index when the new work creates a durable concept, changes the recommended entry point, or fills a missing category. Group entries by domain and give each a short description; do not turn the index into another concept document.

lines.text: - commit author dates go stale the same way: the working-copy commit is author-stamped at *creation*, edits never restamp it. when the author date should say when the work was actually edited (the files' mtime), make the commit through git in the colocated repo (`GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=… git commit`, then any jj command auto-imports it) and `jj abandon` the stale change. jj itself cannot set timestamps: [`vcs/jj/rewrites.md`](/vcs/jj/rewrites.md#backdating-a-fresh-commit-stale-working-copy-dates)

lines.text: - **jj has its own DSL for revsets and templates — do not guess syntax.** Consult `jj help -k revsets` and `jj help -k templates` before writing `-r` or `-T` arguments.

lines.subject: agents.md: jj template mini-guide
lines.text: - Revset DAG operators: `::@` (ancestors of @), `@::` (descendants of @), `::` (all visible), `x..y` (range). No `::~`.

lines.subject: agents.md: jj template mini-guide
lines.text: - Template fields are bare keywords, not object properties: `change_id.short()` not `commit.change_id.short()`. `description.first_line()` not `commit.description.first_line()`.

lines.subject: agents.md: jj template mini-guide
lines.text: - String concatenation in templates uses `++`.

lines.subject: agents.md: jj template mini-guide
lines.text: - compact log: `jj log --limit 10 -r '::@' -T 'change_id.short() ++ " " ++ description.first_line() ++ "\n"'`

lines.text: # jj-hunk

lines.subject: docs: add jj-hunk mini-guide to AGENTS.md
code: author jj-hunk reference; slim AGENTS.md section to ambient cut
lines.text: - `jj-hunk` selects individual hunks of a diff and commits/splits/squashes only those. it is the tool for logical changes intermingled **within** files, and for clean hunk commits without a TTY (agents, CI). when file boundaries already align with the logical change, plain `jj commit -m "<msg>" <files>` is simpler — prefer it.

lines.subject: code: author jj-hunk reference; slim AGENTS.md section to ambient cut
lines.text: - spec shape: `{"files": {"<path>": {"ids": ["hunk-<sha256>", ...]}}}`. use **full** `hunk-<sha256>` IDs: short prefixes silently match nothing and `jj-hunk commit` happily creates an empty commit with no error.

lines.subject: code: author jj-hunk reference; slim AGENTS.md section to ambient cut
lines.text: - always dry-run before committing: `jj-hunk list --spec '<spec>'` must list exactly the hunks you expect.

lines.subject: code: author jj-hunk reference; slim AGENTS.md section to ambient cut
lines.text: - wholesale-rewritten files don't hunk-split into clean intermediates: restore the file from the parent rev, apply the minimal change, commit, then write the full version back and commit again.
